## Design

### 2026-10-09: October 10: Completed the schematic at 3 AM

**8h**

October 10: Completed the schematic at 3 AM

Well, it's 3 AM and I'm a premed student sneakily using my sister's laptop to design a circuit board.
And somehow I have done it. The entire schematic is finished!

Setup (aka struggles)
I first installed KiCad and unzipped the Care Package as shown in the guide. Then I spent a good few minutes being sure that I had unzipped it incorrectly, since all I could see was one library; however, it was actually correct.
When I added the footprint library. Upon opening the folder, it appeared to be entirely empty and I was trying to figure out but it worked somehow even I don't  really know what I did anyways... I also noticed some small arrows drifting, so I got rid of them thinking they must be rubbish ...turned out to be my power symbols and i had to import them all over again.  I had also connected my GND and 3.3V inversely. A real board would have been very sad that took my time as well.

What I actually built

The XIAO-ESP32-C3 as the brain, plus power symbols
Net labels on its pins so I didn’t have to draw a million wires: SDA, SCL, DHT, BTN1, BTN2
Two push buttons (one side to a label, one side to GND)
A 4-pin header for the OLED screen
An 8-pin header for the MPU6050 (I only wired the first 4 pins)
The DHT11 temperature sensor

Footprints
I assigned footprints, that is to say the real shapes that the components will take on the board; the chip received the XIAO footprint from the Care Package, the headers were given normal 2.54mm pin header footprints, the buttons were given a 6mm push button footprint and the DHT11 was given its sensor footprint.

Next I opened the PCB Editor and loaded all my components in and drew the board outline, arranged everything and route the traces.
So next up will be maybe making star shape I hope you'll have good luck and perhaps go to sleep

### 2026-10-11: October 11: Star outline, ground pour redo, Gerbers and GitHub

**8h**

October 11: Star outline, ground pour redo, Gerbers and GitHub

Yesterday the board was completely routed without any errors, but it still ended up as a dull rectangle. Since Starbie should be something special, I decided to redraw the outline. (bad decision)
![1000032219](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/gfWl2tMDbbFllUPCOWxRpQb4XDb3SDLx/a8343bdb994404cb29a5fed39acec4326ee3293233c7e3f098bbd2450021708f.jpg)

Drawing the star
I marked the star on the Edge. To do this I used the edge cut layer with line tool, copying the ladder-type edges from the guide's picture. When I first tried it I got 'line, blank, line, blank' rather than chaining and it took up most of the time to get a hold of.
![1000032220](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/gfWl2tMDbbFllUPCOWxRpQb4XDb3SDLx/8fe4891b27225261d42032a11857efa1d7b073410b1efebc168adcd20500f566.jpg)

The design checker complained as some parts were poking outside the star and the copper pour no longer matched the new shape.
![1000032222](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/gfWl2tMDbbFllUPCOWxRpQb4XDb3SDLx/5ab029286c884282e13f421452b8a3f41eca85be127a1b0f46ca48e84b2c514f.jpg)

 I tried dragging parts one at a time, but they kept snapping back to where they were. What worked was making the star bigger to fit everything inside but this thought came to me after I had tried every possible way to fit the components inside the star. Then I drew a new GND zone on the front copper layer.
![1000032204](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/gfWl2tMDbbFllUPCOWxRpQb4XDb3SDLx/0019d0a919d2311f67fe3c6ab445fb78e97fbcca91adaab3a3d9af029403eb41.jpg)

One more error😞
The checker pointed out that the board outline was not a closed shape since there was a small gap along the edge of the star, so I corrected this and the DRC displayed zero errors with only five harmless warnings about track ends 🙃. I then exported the Gerber files and the drill files into a gerbers folder.
![1000032221](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/gfWl2tMDbbFllUPCOWxRpQb4XDb3SDLx/4196aaddfba2a3575de9ae786b9408afac1ca149681a3949c442c21fa67fdff7.jpg)

I also created a public repository named Starbie and uploaded the KiCad project files along with the gerbers folder.

### 2026-10-20: Oct 19 and 20: Starbie Edits!

**9h**

Oct 19 and 20: Starbie Edits!
How it started: I was looking through my project yesterday and compared it with the guide and idk but my starbie wasnt starbeing i did noticed it before but didnt had time to redo stuff so finally I sat down today and was like "Right, let's get our PCB to look more like the guides". The 3D models weren't appearing correctly at all and nothing was quite right. So I checked the schematic (that was all spot on) and then went back to the PCB editor and spotted the problems with my footprints so i redid them imported and aligned the custom 3D models and completely reworked the layout from the ground up.

![Screenshot 389](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/gfWl2tMDbbFllUPCOWxRpQb4XDb3SDLx/2d39a82e10229cba5cff2d19b44f7ea324e7ae5724e0d2a49270418b2f5dd577.png)

![Screenshot 397](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/gfWl2tMDbbFllUPCOWxRpQb4XDb3SDLx/e5d481b9e075020a66f7430d5aa3a5eda9a94251232050125e0560e5e41e052b.png)
Another problem  was that a couple of components needed to be re-oriented. For example, the OLED header (Conn_01x04) was flipped relative to the reference, which messed up the GND, VDD, SDA and SCL pin order.

Here’s how I got everything locked in:
Rotated the OLED header 180 degrees using R so the pinout matched the reference.
Sorted out all the DRC errors on my Starbie board. Rerouted the SDA and SCL tracks off the J2 header, connected the +3.3V and GND nets together with vias and set the GND fill to solid pad connections. Cleaned up some of the old tracks and routed the main signal paths on F.Cu (Front Copper), using vias to jump over to B.Cu (Back Copper) where the paths crossed.

Cleared out the remaining DRC errors (including pad centre alignment gaps on pad 12 for +3.3V).
Fixed the ground pour issue: having drawn the zone boundary around the star edge cuts (Edge.Cuts) cuz my star was not able to fit all components anymore and increasing its size just left empty spaces in between. I pressed B to recalculate and flood fill the solid copper plane across the board.
With all the yellow DRC markers cleared and the 3D models rendering perfectly, the starboard is now looking exactly as the guide has it and is ready to go!
